headline: Mecka, a start-up that records how people use their hands so robots can learn from it, has raised $60 million.
score_reason: Kept at pool score 5: a notable round, but the revenue figures are the company's own.
importance_line: What changed is that investors are paying to fix robots' shortage of real-world experience data, which matters to people who may one day work beside such machines, then to robot makers that need training data, and the doubt is that the revenue figures and forecast are Mecka's own and no outside check is reported.
summary: Pulse 2.0 reports that Mecka's Series B round (a mid-stage investment round) was led by Sequoia Capital, with Nvidia, Microsoft's M12 fund, Qualcomm Ventures and Samsung joining as new investors, and will pay for more recording equipment, research and robot deployments. The company, which says it supplies robot-training data to several leading robotics labs, says its run-rate revenue passed $100 million in June 2026 and expects about $300 million by the end of the year.
notes: Funding story, no machine shown doing a task.
